items.title: How khipus indicated labour contributions in an Andean village: An explanation of colour banding, seriation and ethnocategories
items.note: Uses archival testimony and interviews from Santiago de Anchucaya, where khipus recorded communal labour into the 1940s, to explain colour banding and seriation.

items.title: Inka History in Knots: Reading Khipus as Primary Sources
items.note: Synthesis arguing that khipus, read mainly through numerical and structural patterns, can serve as primary sources for Inka administrative and social history.

items.title: Hidden Texts of the Andes: Deciphering the 'Khipus' (Cord Writing) of Peru
items.note: Leverhulme-funded project (2017 to 2021) on village khipus, khipu boards and paper archives used to decode communal labour records.

items.title: Writing with Twisted Cords: The Inscriptive Capacity of Andean Khipus
items.note: Reports two narrative khipus kept at Collata with about 95 distinct sign combinations of fibre, colour and ply, and proposes a partly logosyllabic reading.

items.title: Toward the Decipherment of a Set of Mid-Colonial Khipus from the Santa Valley, Coastal Peru
items.note: Matches six Santa Valley khipus to a 1670s Spanish census and argues that colour and cord attachment encode names and moiety affiliation.

items.title: Guggenheim Fellowship (US$55,000) for decoding khipus
items.note: US$55,000 fellowship for Hyland's work interpreting the coloured animal-fibre cords of narrative khipus as a writing system.

items.title: The Invention of Taxation in the Inka Empire
items.note: Analyses khipus excavated at the Inkawasi storehouse under produce and identifies a recurring 'fixed number' formula interpreted as a tax deduction.

items.title: Toward a Grammar of the Inka Khipu: Investigating the Production of Non-numerical Signs
items.note: Applies computational and statistical methods to the khipu corpus to identify recurring paired non-numerical signs and their production conventions.

items.title: Calendars in Knotted Cords: New Evidence on How Khipus Captured Time in Nineteenth-Century Cuzco and Beyond
items.who: J. C. de la Puente Luna
items.note: Reconstructs calendar-demographic khipus near Cuzco from a nineteenth-century memoir, showing how cords recorded dated events within a twelve-month cycle.

items.title: Subject Indicators and the Decipherment of Genre on Andean Khipus
items.note: Argues that particular cord features served as subject indicators marking a khipu's genre, drawing on Julio C. Tello's notes and ethnographic evidence.

items.title: Khipu Field Guide
items.note: Open site rendering schematic drawings and analyses of several hundred khipus from public data; online by November 2020 per the earliest web archive capture.

items.title: Khipu Transcription Typologies: A Corpus-Based Study of the Textos Andinos
items.note: Builds a syntactically annotated corpus of sixteenth-century khipu transcriptions and applies multivariate statistics to classify 'paper khipus' by type.

items.title: The Open Khipu Repository, v1.0.0
items.note: First versioned release of an open, unified database of Inka-style khipus merging the Harvard Khipu Database and other recording schemes.

items.title: Khipus, Khipu Boards, and Sacred Texts: Toward a Philology of Andean Knotted Cords
items.who: S. Hyland, S. Bennison and W. P. Hyland
items.note: Pairs khipus and khipu boards with written religious texts from Huarochirí communities to propose a philological method for reading cords.

items.title: khipulab/renaming: replication code for the KH khipu naming convention
items.note: Code that assigns KH numbers and crosswalks earlier identifiers, implemented in OKR v2.0.0 so specimens can be matched across recording schemes.

items.title: Heritage Science Contribution to the Understanding of Meaningful Khipu Colours
items.note: First scientific analysis of khipu dyes and mordants, identifying colourants so that colour categories can be tested on material rather than visual grounds.

items.title: Two khipus among antiquities returned to Peru at the Los Angeles consulate
items.who: US federal authorities and Consulate of Peru
items.note: Two khipus surrendered by a private gallery to federal investigators were repatriated to Peru with other antiquities.

items.title: Knotted Survivors: Endangered Khipu Traditions of the Peruvian Andes
items.note: British Academy-funded project (2023 to 2024) to document endangered community khipu traditions; its listed output is the 2025 isotope study of KH0631.

items.title: A New Naming Convention for Andean Khipus
items.who: C. Brezine, J. Clindaniel, I. Ghezzi et al.
items.note: Proposes replacing researcher-based khipu names with neutral KH#### identifiers to link specimens to their places of origin and unify catalogues.

items.title: How Can Data Science Contribute to Understanding the Khipu Code?
items.note: Characterises arithmetic and structural regularities across the whole public corpus, setting a quantitative baseline that non-numerical readings must exceed.

items.title: colorful-ai-khipukamayuq
items.note: Notebooks accompanying 'Colorful Insights from an AI Khipukamayuq', which trains models on OKR data to test how cord colour patterns relate to meaning.

items.title: New Insights on Cord Attachment and Social Hierarchy in Six Khipus from the Santa Valley, Peru
items.note: Re-examines the six Santa Valley khipus matched to a colonial census and argues that patterns of cord attachment record social hierarchy.

items.title: A Numerical Connection Between Two Khipus
items.note: Shows a complex numerical relationship between two khipus excavated together near Arica and identifies a knot form that may mark an individual maker.

items.title: Inka Numbers, Khipu, and Yupana: a Reanalysis
items.who: C. Florio and K. A. Overmann
items.note: Reinterprets the 1615 yupana drawing and argues that Inka numeration was likely non-positional, questioning the standard place-value reading.

items.title: Khipu-Biblio Cross-Reference (KBCR) Resource
items.note: Error-corrected listing linking each known khipu to the publications that mention it, keyed to Khipu Field Guide identifiers; described in Advances in Archaeological Practice (2025).

items.title: Knotted Survivors: Documenting the Ancient Khipu Traditions of Jucul, Peru
items.venue: British Museum Endangered Material Knowledge Programme
items.note: Arcadia-funded British Museum grant to conserve Jucul's 97 community khipus, including a 68-metre example, and record knowledge holders' explanations.

items.title: Stable isotope evidence for the participation of commoners in Inka khipu production
items.who: S. Hyland, C. Lee, H. Koon et al.
items.note: Isotope analysis of human hair forming the primary cord of khipu KH0631 indicates a commoner's diet, challenging the view that only elites made khipus.

items.title: The Open Khipu Repository, v2.1.0
items.note: Adds 72 newly recorded khipus (KH0631 to KH0702) after advisory board review and a master KH number registry.

items.title: Meaningful matters in the Andean khipu technology
items.note: Studies khipu fibres, dyes and thread wrappings as carriers of meaning, with a companion Zenodo dataset of morphological records and sampling areas.

items.title: Knot Tricks: What Mathematical Knot Theory Can Reveal about the Structure of Khipu Knot Encoding
items.note: Applies mathematical knot theory to khipu knot types to clarify which structural distinctions the knotting system could encode.

items.title: String Theories: Astral Numerology, Scientific Internationalism, and Inca Quipu Decipherment at the Göteborg Museum
items.note: Historicises Nordenskiöld's discredited 1925 astronomical reading of quipus, examining why claimed decipherments gained and lost authority.

items.title: Haptic Khipu: Studying a Tactile Archive
items.who: A. Boswell, J. Cobo Betancourt et al. (UC Santa Barbara)
items.note: Radiocarbon dates (c. 1500 to 1643 CE), hyperspectral and UV imaging of a khipu in the UCSB AD&A Museum, carried out in 2025 and published online.

items.title: Structural Pattern Mining in Inka Khipus: Unsupervised Clustering, Provenance Classification, and a Computational Validation of the Santa Valley Match
items.note: Machine-learning analysis of 619 OKR khipus that reproduces the Santa Valley moiety pattern from public data and finds knot-sequence n-grams add no provenance signal.
